quests.hint: Frozen water; the thing you 'break' to make people feel comfortable.
quests.explanation: 'Break the ice' means do or say something that makes people feel relaxed at the start of a social situation.
quests.textToSpeak: He told a joke to break the ___ at the start of the awkward dinner.
quests.correctAnswer: He told a joke to break the ice at the start of the awkward dinner.
quests.contextClue: An awkward dinner needs a way to relax people.

quests.hint: A sweet baked dessert, used in a phrase for something very easy.
quests.explanation: 'A piece of cake' means something very easy. It is an informal idiom.
quests.textToSpeak: I thought the exam would be hard, but it was a piece of ___.
quests.correctAnswer: I thought the exam would be hard, but it was a piece of cake.
quests.contextClue: 'I thought it would be hard, but' signals the surprise of ease.

quests.hint: A body part used in a phrase for something very expensive.
quests.explanation: 'Cost an arm and a leg' means cost a huge amount of money. It is an informal idiom.
quests.textToSpeak: That watch looks lovely, but it costs an arm and a ___.
quests.correctAnswer: That watch looks lovely, but it costs an arm and a leg.
quests.contextClue: A lovely watch with an enormous price.

quests.hint: A way of hiding what something really is.
quests.explanation: 'A blessing in disguise' is something that seems bad at first but turns out to be good.
quests.textToSpeak: Losing that job felt terrible, but it turned out to be a blessing in ___.
quests.correctAnswer: Losing that job felt terrible, but it turned out to be a blessing in disguise.
quests.contextClue: Losing the job felt terrible but later proved positive.

quests.hint: Dried stalks of grain; one extra piece breaks a camel's back in a saying.
quests.explanation: 'The last straw' is the final problem that makes you lose patience.
quests.textToSpeak: When the bus was late again, that was the last ___; I bought a bike.
quests.correctAnswer: When the bus was late again, that was the last straw; I bought a bike.
quests.contextClue: Repeated lateness leads to a final decision.

quests.hint: The part of your body above your neck.
quests.explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' means describe exactly what the problem is.
quests.textToSpeak: You've hit the nail on the ___; that's exactly the problem.
quests.correctAnswer: You've hit the nail on the head; that's exactly the problem.
quests.contextClue: The listener has identified the exact problem.

quests.hint: The edge or brink of something.
quests.explanation: 'On the verge of' means very close to doing or feeling something: 'on the verge of tears'.
quests.textToSpeak: She was on the ___ of tears when she walked in and saw the surprise party.
quests.correctAnswer: She was on the verge of tears when she walked in and saw the surprise party.
quests.contextClue: A surprise party brings her close to crying.

quests.hint: The area marked out for a game like tennis.
quests.explanation: 'The ball is in your court' means it is your turn to act or decide.
quests.textToSpeak: I've made my offer, so now the ball is in your ___.
quests.correctAnswer: I've made my offer, so now the ball is in your court.
quests.contextClue: The speaker has done their part and is waiting.

quests.hint: The bright object in the night sky.
quests.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' means very rarely.
quests.textToSpeak: We only see each other once in a blue ___.
quests.correctAnswer: We only see each other once in a blue moon.
quests.contextClue: Seeing someone only rarely.

quests.hint: A container you carry things in; in this idiom, where a secret is kept.
quests.explanation: 'Let the cat out of the bag' means reveal a secret by accident.
quests.textToSpeak: I promised not to tell anyone, but my brother let the cat out of the ___.
quests.correctAnswer: I promised not to tell anyone, but my brother let the cat out of the bag.
quests.contextClue: A promise not to tell was broken.

quests.hint: A vessel that floats on water; you can 'miss' it if you're too late.
quests.explanation: 'Miss the boat' means lose an opportunity by acting too late.
quests.textToSpeak: If you don't apply today, you'll miss the ___; the deadline is tonight.
quests.correctAnswer: If you don't apply today, you'll miss the boat; the deadline is tonight.
quests.contextClue: A deadline tonight warns of a lost chance.

quests.hint: Places where two walls meet; 'cutting' them means doing things cheaply.
quests.explanation: 'Cut corners' means do something in a cheaper or quicker way, often lowering the quality.
quests.textToSpeak: They cut ___ to save money, and now the wall is already cracking.
quests.correctAnswer: They cut corners to save money, and now the wall is already cracking.
quests.contextClue: Saving money led to a cracking wall.

quests.hint: A barrier around a garden; sitting on it means you haven't decided.
quests.explanation: 'On the fence' means undecided between two choices.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm still on the ___ about accepting the job; the pay is great but the hours are long.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm still on the fence about accepting the job; the pay is great but the hours are long.
quests.contextClue: Good pay is balanced against long hours.

quests.hint: A unit of distance; in this idiom it means extra effort.
quests.explanation: 'Go the extra mile' means make more effort than is expected.
quests.textToSpeak: That waiter really went the extra ___ to make our anniversary special.
quests.correctAnswer: That waiter really went the extra mile to make our anniversary special.
quests.contextClue: The waiter did more than was required.

quests.hint: A very short period of time.
quests.explanation: 'On the spur of the moment' means suddenly, without planning.
quests.textToSpeak: We booked the trip on the spur of the ___; we didn't even look at hotels.
quests.correctAnswer: We booked the trip on the spur of the moment; we didn't even look at hotels.
quests.contextClue: They booked without checking details.

quests.hint: A huge body of salt water.
quests.explanation: 'A drop in the ocean' means a very small amount compared with what is needed.
quests.textToSpeak: Our donation is just a drop in the ___ compared to what the hospital needs.
quests.correctAnswer: Our donation is just a drop in the ocean compared to what the hospital needs.
quests.contextClue: A donation is tiny compared to the needs.

quests.hint: A huge piece of floating ice, mostly hidden under the water.
quests.explanation: 'The tip of the iceberg' means a small visible part of a much bigger problem.
quests.textToSpeak: The errors we've found so far are only the tip of the ___.
quests.correctAnswer: The errors we've found so far are only the tip of the iceberg.
quests.contextClue: The errors found so far suggest more hidden ones.

quests.hint: Rows of written words; hidden meanings sit between them.
quests.explanation: 'Read between the lines' means understand meanings that are not stated directly.
quests.textToSpeak: She said she was 'fine', but if you read between the ___, she was clearly upset.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she was 'fine', but if you read between the lines, she was clearly upset.
quests.contextClue: 'Fine' did not match how she seemed.

quests.hint: The colour of a clear sky.
quests.explanation: 'Out of the blue' means suddenly and unexpectedly.
quests.textToSpeak: I hadn't heard from him in ten years, and then he called me out of the ___.
quests.correctAnswer: I hadn't heard from him in ten years, and then he called me out of the blue.
quests.contextClue: A call after ten years of silence.

quests.hint: Wet, with rain falling.
quests.explanation: 'Save for a rainy day' means keep money for a time of need.
quests.textToSpeak: It's sensible to save a little each month for a ___ day.
quests.correctAnswer: It's sensible to save a little each month for a rainy day.
quests.contextClue: Saving monthly suggests preparing for hard times.

quests.hint: Something unpleasant that you decide to accept.
quests.explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means accept something unpleasant and get on with it.
quests.textToSpeak: It will be awkward, but I'll have to bite the ___ and tell him the truth.
quests.correctAnswer: It will be awkward, but I'll have to bite the bullet and tell him the truth.
quests.contextClue: The speaker decides to do the awkward thing.

quests.hint: A state of fairness between two things; here, time for each part of your life.
quests.explanation: 'Strike a balance' means find a fair middle position between two things. 'Work-life balance' is a related phrase.
quests.textToSpeak: It's hard to strike a ___ between work and a social life.
quests.correctAnswer: It's hard to strike a balance between work and a social life.
quests.contextClue: Work and social life need to share time.

quests.hint: A final decision or judgment based on evidence.
quests.explanation: 'Draw a conclusion' means decide something based on evidence. 'Jump to conclusions' means decide too quickly.
quests.textToSpeak: Don't draw a ___ until you've seen all the evidence.
quests.correctAnswer: Don't draw a conclusion until you've seen all the evidence.
quests.contextClue: Waiting for all the evidence before judging.

quests.hint: The force that keeps something moving or growing.
quests.explanation: 'Gain momentum' means get faster or stronger as it develops.
quests.textToSpeak: After the first victory, the campaign started to gain ___ and support grew daily.
quests.correctAnswer: After the first victory, the campaign started to gain momentum and support grew daily.
quests.contextClue: Growing support follows an early win.

quests.hint: Be as good as people expected.
quests.explanation: 'Live up to' means be as good as people hoped or said: 'live up to expectations'.
quests.textToSpeak: The film didn't ___ up to all the hype, to be honest.
quests.correctAnswer: The film didn't live up to all the hype, to be honest.
quests.contextClue: Hype creates high expectations.

quests.hint: Succeed in doing something difficult.
quests.explanation: 'Pull off' means succeed in something difficult. The object can come before 'off': 'pull it off'.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't think we could ___ it off, but the event went perfectly.
quests.correctAnswer: I didn't think we could pull it off, but the event went perfectly.
quests.contextClue: Doubt is followed by success.

quests.hint: Study a topic by looking at books or websites.
quests.explanation: 'Read up on' means study a subject by reading about it. It is informal and common before trips or exams.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm going to ___ up on the local customs before we travel to Japan.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm going to read up on the local customs before we travel to Japan.
quests.contextClue: Preparing for travel involves learning about a place.

quests.hint: The past participle of a verb meaning to exclude something.
quests.explanation: 'Rule out' means exclude a possibility: 'they haven't ruled out arson'. Rule is a regular verb.
quests.textToSpeak: The police have not ___ out the possibility of a fire.
quests.correctAnswer: The police have not ruled out the possibility of a fire.
quests.contextClue: Without exclusion, the fire remains possible.

quests.hint: Reduce in size or extent.
quests.explanation: 'Scale down' means make something smaller. The opposite is 'scale up'.
quests.textToSpeak: Because of budget cuts, we had to ___ down the project.
quests.correctAnswer: Because of budget cuts, we had to scale down the project.
quests.contextClue: Budget cuts force a reduction.

quests.hint: The past tense of a verb meaning each give a small amount of money.
quests.explanation: 'Chip in' means contribute money or effort together. It is a regular verb: chip, chipped.
quests.textToSpeak: We all ___ in to buy her a leaving gift.
quests.correctAnswer: We all chipped in to buy her a leaving gift.
quests.contextClue: A group gift needs everyone's share.
